sources.title: 15A NCAC 10B .0303 (open seasons — trapping)

sources.title: N.C.G.S. § 113-129(7a) (fur-bearing animals defined)
sources.notes: Official statute listing fur-bearing animals: beaver, mink, muskrat, nutria, otter, skunk, weasel, and bobcat/opossum/raccoon when trapped. Ringtail is NOT listed and is excluded from this dataset.

license_summary.trapping_license: A trapping license is required to trap furbearers. Coyote trapping is also allowed during local fox trapping seasons in counties with locally established fox seasons.
license_summary.depredation: Outside the trapping season, animals can be trapped only under a Depredation Permit (free, from a Wildlife Enforcement Officer, Wildlife District Biologist, or Licensed Wildlife Control Agent); landowners whose property has been damaged by beavers may take beaver on their property anytime by any lawful method without a depredation permit, and no depredation permit is required to trap nutria east of I-77 (depredation provisions are noted here, not modeled as seasons).

verification.confirmation_notes: Verified 2026-11-15 against the official NC 2026-2027 Regulations Digest (Trapping Regulations and Small Game & Other Seasons, via eRegulations), the NCWRC Carolina Furbearer Newsletter Fall/Winter 2026-2027, and 15A NCAC 10B .0303. All modeled rows confirmed: statewide trapping Oct. 1, 2026–Feb. 28, 2027 for the 14 listed species; nutria no closed season east of I-77; raccoon/opossum/bobcat hunting Oct. 12, 2026–Feb. 28, 2027 with digest limits; fox/bobcat/otter pelt tagging requirements; five-county January fox trapping season added from the digest.
known_gaps: Fox trapping and hunting seasons set by county local law (~55 counties) are not modeled county-by-county; the NCWRC 'Fox Hunting and Trapping Seasons' publication (ncwildlife.gov/foxseasons, updated Aug. 19, 2026) is image-based and its per-county tables could not be machine-read. The statewide season and the digest's five-county January season are modeled.

The digest also provides no closed hunting season on private lands for coyote, groundhog, nutria, striped skunk, and armadillo (and year-round beaver take by firearm/bow with landowner permission); consistent with this file's existing design, only dated hunting seasons are modeled as rows, and those provisions are covered in the license summary and notes.
Scientific names are standard taxonomy, not stated in NCWRC regulations.
